service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 68-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, ICD-10-CM E10.65. Fasting C-peptide is undetectable (below the lab's lower limit of normal) with a concurrent fasting glucose of 162 mg/dL. He completed a comprehensive diabetes education program 3 years ago and has used multiple daily injections (basal plus three prandial injections daily) with frequent self-adjustment of doses for 4 years. His meter download shows an average of 5.2 glucose checks per day over the last 2 months. His HbA1c on this regimen is 8.1%. The pump is ordered by an endocrinologist who manages over 100 CSII patients with a team of diabetes nurses, educators, and a dietitian. Request: external insulin pump (CSII) and supplies for home use.
rationale_note: Criterion A fully met; C-peptide undetectable with valid glucose; HbA1c 8.1%.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 74-year-old woman with long-standing insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease with a measured creatinine clearance of 45 mL/min. Fasting C-peptide is 180% of the laboratory's lower limit of normal, drawn with a concurrent fasting glucose of 190 mg/dL; GAD65 antibodies are negative. She completed a comprehensive diabetes education program and has been on four insulin injections daily with frequent self-adjustment for 2 years. Meter logs show an average of 4.6 checks per day over the last 2 months. On this regimen she has had recurring hypoglycemia (three to four episodes below 54 mg/dL per month). An endocrinologist experienced with many CSII patients, working with a CSII nurse, educator, and dietitian, orders an external insulin pump for home use.
rationale_note: C-peptide 180% of LLN fails the usual 110% cutoff but meets the 200% cutoff because creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min; recurring hypoglycemia satisfies Criterion A.

vignette: 70-year-old man with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and a creatinine clearance of 82 mL/min. Fasting C-peptide is 150% of the laboratory's lower limit of normal with a concurrent fasting glucose of 150 mg/dL; GAD65, IA-2, and ZnT8 antibodies are all negative. He completed comprehensive diabetes education, has used three to four insulin injections daily with frequent self-adjustment for 18 months, and his meter shows an average of 4.8 checks per day over the past 2 months. HbA1c is 8.6%. An endocrinologist experienced with many CSII patients and supported by a CSII team orders an external insulin pump.
rationale_note: Normal renal function, so the 110% cutoff applies; C-peptide 150% of LLN and antibodies negative.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 67-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes; fasting C-peptide is undetectable with a concurrent fasting glucose of 140 mg/dL. She completed a comprehensive diabetes education program and has used multiple daily injections (four per day) with frequent self-adjustment for 6 years. Her HbA1c is 7.9% and she reports wide fluctuations in pre-meal glucose. Her meter download for the past 2 months shows an average of 3.1 glucose checks per day. An endocrinologist who manages many CSII patients with a team of nurses, educators, and dietitians orders an external insulin pump.
rationale_note: Self-testing averages 3.1/day over the prior 2 months; at least 4/day is required.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 65-year-old man with type 1 diabetes who has used an insulin pump for 9 years through his employer plan and just enrolled in Medicare. His meter records for the month before Medicare enrollment show an average of 4.3 glucose checks per day. GAD65 antibodies are positive; no C-peptide test is on file. His endocrinologist, who manages over 80 pump patients with a team of diabetes nurses, educators, and a dietitian, orders an external insulin pump and supplies for home use under Medicare.
rationale_note: Criterion B: on a pump before Medicare enrollment with >= 4 checks/day the month before; antibody positive substitutes for C-peptide.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 71-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes; fasting C-peptide is below the lab's lower limit of normal with concurrent fasting glucose of 132 mg/dL. She completed a comprehensive diabetes education program and has used four daily insulin injections with frequent self-adjustment for 3 years; meter data show 5.5 checks per day over the past 2 months. Her HbA1c on this regimen is 7.0%. Her physician documents no history of recurring hypoglycemia, stable pre-meal glucose values, no dawn phenomenon (fasting values 100-140 mg/dL), and no severe glycemic excursions. She wants a pump for convenience. An endocrinologist experienced with many CSII patients and a CSII team orders an external insulin pump.
rationale_note: Boundary: HbA1c exactly 7.0% is not > 7.0%, and none of the other qualifying glycemic criteria are present.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 59-year-old woman on Medicare through disability with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and chronic intractable lower-extremity spasticity. Over the past 8 weeks she tried oral baclofen at maximum dose plus tizanidine; spasticity remained uncontrolled (Modified Ashworth 4 in both legs) and she had intolerable sedation. A trial intrathecal bolus of baclofen reduced her Ashworth scores to 1-2 for 8 hours. She has no allergy to baclofen, no active infection, adequate body size for the device, and no other implanted programmable devices. Her neurologist requests implantation of a programmable infusion pump for intrathecal baclofen.
rationale_note: Intrathecal baclofen pump: 8-week oral trial failed, favorable intrathecal test dose, no contraindications.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 63-year-old man on Medicare through disability with spastic paraparesis after a thoracic spinal cord injury. A 10-week trial of oral baclofen and dantrolene failed to control spasticity. A trial intrathecal dose of baclofen produced marked improvement. He has no drug allergy, no active infection, and adequate body size. He has had a programmable implanted spinal cord stimulator for neuropathic pain for 4 years, which will remain in place. His physiatrist requests implantation of an intrathecal baclofen infusion pump.
rationale_note: Implanted programmable spinal cord stimulator: implantation is contraindicated with other implanted programmable devices.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 69-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer and severe intractable abdominal and back pain despite high-dose oral and transdermal opioids with intolerable sedation. A temporary intrathecal catheter trial of morphine gave good pain relief with acceptable side effects, and he accepts the therapy. His oncologist documents an estimated life expectancy of about 6 weeks. He has no active infection, drug allergy, or other implanted devices. His pain physician requests implantation of an intrathecal opioid infusion pump.
rationale_note: Life expectancy about 6 weeks, below the required 3 months, despite a successful trial.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 66-year-old woman with severe chronic intractable low back and leg pain of nonmalignant origin after three spinal surgeries. Her history documents inadequate relief and intolerable side effects from systemic opioids and adjuvant medications, plus completed behavioral pain management. She has no life-limiting illness, no active infection, no drug allergy, adequate body size, and no other implanted devices. Her pain physician requests implantation of an intrathecal morphine infusion pump. The record contains the history, medication list, and psychology note, and no documentation of any intraspinal opioid trial.
rationale_note: No record of a preliminary trial with a temporary intraspinal catheter; nothing contradicts it.

service: Infusion pumps (external CSII insulin pumps and implantable intrathecal pumps)
vignette: 72-year-old man with type 1 diabetes; fasting C-peptide is undetectable with a concurrent fasting glucose of 170 mg/dL. He completed a comprehensive diabetes education program and has used four daily insulin injections with frequent self-adjustment for 5 years. His HbA1c is 8.4%. An endocrinologist who manages many CSII patients with a team of CSII-knowledgeable nurses, educators, and dietitians orders an external insulin pump. The submitted records include the lab results and clinic notes; there are no meter downloads, logs, or notes about how often he checks his glucose.
rationale_note: Glucose self-testing frequency is not documented anywhere; other Criterion A elements are met.
